sound.checked_and_sound: (1) The AM-GM step is correct: every factor is at least 1-q >= 1/2, the expectation of the round product factorises under within-round independence, the bound holds for each fixed q and therefore for the equal mixture of full products; I found no error in PROOF steps 1 to 9 under their stated assumptions. (2) Needed are joint independence of cells within a round, independence of each round from earlier rounds, and each round's own suite mean obeying the null; identical cell laws across rounds are sufficient but not necessary, and an average-over-rounds null is not enough (finding 1, with exact counterexamples). (3) Ville is applied correctly at round ends (W_0=1, inclusive threshold 40, a cap only shrinks the event) and first-stop keeps both directional bounds because each declared verdict is a subset of its own crossing event. (4) At round ends the product commutes, so there is no dependence on cell order or on any schedule; the only residual dependence is on round order, and only when laws are not stationary. (5) A weighted suite mean works if cell stakes are proportional to weights (lam_c = lam*w_c/w_max gives a bound base of 1 + lam*(Delta_w+delta)/(N*w_max)), so PROOF.md:17 is slightly too strong: cell-dependent stakes retarget the null rather than break validity. Repeating cell c k_c times per round is valid only for the k-weighted mean; against the unweighted null it fails (nine +1 cells run twice and eleven -1 cells once give round factors 5.13 and 2.61), so every round must hold every cell exactly once. (6) The mid-round counterexample is correct: wealth 151874368379777/5642219814912 = 26.92 at pair 8 and 316547748620285/7522959753216 = 42.08 at pair 9, complete-round PASS factors 0.465 and 0.036, BLOCK factors 0.582 and 0.085; decide gives PASS at pair 9 with pairwise looks and INCONCLUSIVE at 400 by rounds, and a terminal partial round is indeed an unprotected look. (7) Scoring an errored pair as -1 for PASS and +1 for BLOCK keeps each test valid: each wealth is monotone in d, so the scored path is pointwise at most the path under any fill-in of the errored pairs, the crossing event shrinks whatever causes the errors, and both tests still cannot cross together; the errored pair must stay in its round as a factor, never be dropped or replaced. Enumeration check: an independently written absorbing recursion over rounds equalled balanced.enumerate_balanced exactly (N=5, cap 100, heterogeneous three-support laws; all probabilities and expected pairs equal as fractions), and the stationary even law at N=20 reproduced 0.009034 / 0.004849. I did not run run_all.py or s1c_study.py and wrote nothing in the repository; check scripts are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ajay--claude-spares-spare-8K9guD/39ca2335-7a5a-47d9-a374-69d92a47e1d0/scratchpad/ (chk2.py, chk3.py).

Proof: the AM-GM step, non-negativity of every factor, linearity for the fixed mixture and Ville's bound are correct as written, and the mid-round counterexample checks out ((47/36)^9 + (29/18)^9)/2 = 42.08 >= 40. I reproduced in memory, without running the study scripts: N=20 'even' false PASS 0.009034 and false BLOCK 0.004849 (enumerate_balanced), N=10 'even' 0.011279 / 0.005407 with my own float recursion on the spike's frontier, five Table C cells, and the floors (79 pairs pairwise gives 80 at round ends; BLOCK 13 gives 15 and 20). I did not rerun run_all.py or s1c_study.py, and I could not check LangChain's cache behaviour because the package is not installed. (1) Yes: the stage-synchronous pattern in runner.py:1571-1592 can be reused with stage = one round; round-end wealth depends only on the counts of -1 and +1, so any order and parallelism inside a round is free, provided trials are fresh processes that share no state. The gate must verify: manifest and trial seals; every trial matching its scheduled spec with no duplicate or unknown ids; the stored set equal to exactly rounds 1..r times every cell times both arms; every earlier round end recomputed as INCONCLUSIVE; round r decisive or r = max_rounds; and it must look rounds up from the schedule rather than parse pair_id as gate.py:329 and runner.py:1575 do. Two gaps to close there: decide_rounds silently ignores complete rounds supplied after the stopping round (test_s1c.py passes 20 rounds and gets PASS at 80), so 'nothing beyond the stopping round' is the gate's job, and a partial round or a store-write failure must be ERROR. (2) See finding 1. (3) See finding 2. (4) Apply the candidate hard-invariant override at the round end with priority ERROR, then hard-invariant BLOCK, then the statistical verdict; this keeps one legal store shape and costs at most N-1 extra pairs, matching v1, which also waits for the stage. The override sits outside the 2.5% false-BLOCK claim: a candidate with per-trial violation probability v is blocked with probability 1-(1-v)^(candidate trials run), which depends on the stopping round, so the report must give the BLOCK reason separately and state the claim for the statistical BLOCK only. (5) See finding 3. (6) TrialSpec (schema.py:489-492) cannot say 'betting' in interval_method, gives looks the meaning 'cumulative pairs per condition' with () meaning one look, and holds alpha and delta as floats that cannot equal 1/20 and 1/10; fill them with float mirrors and defaults, document them as inert for suite experiment ids, and make every reader take the rule from the SuiteManifest. The binding through experiment_id works only if the suite gate recomputes the digest from the manifest content (rational alpha and delta, stakes, cells, max_rounds, error policy and cap, seed-derivation version); a stored free-text id would let a resealed rule match every spec hash.

refuted.title: Stationarity is load-bearing: with a different seed per (round, cell) the bound is not 'for every manifest, over outcome randomness only'
Independence across cells and rounds must be enforced by seed derivation; a round-level seed or cross-round replay gives 30 to 67 percent error with every marginal on the margin
The per-manifest claim fails as soon as the trial seed changes a cell's success law, and the spike never says what the seed may feed
An errored pair inside a round has no defined treatment; void-and-rerun breaks the bound, worst-case scoring keeps it
'N <= 400' is attainability, not usability: the whole-round cap silently discards up to half the budget
